species.name: Clearfin

dex.text: Pale as a ghost and see-through where it matters, so that you can tell its mood from its blood, except that its blood is clear too. Is not sure why this is a problem for anyone else.
dex.fact: Antarctic icefish are the only adult vertebrates with no haemoglobin: their blood is clear, and the cold, oxygen-rich water lets them get by without it.

species.real: Icefish make up for clear blood with big hearts, wide blood vessels and plenty of blood, and antifreeze proteins in their bodies stop them freezing solid.

species.name: Glaciefin

dex.text: Glassier than ever and twice as calm, glides under the ice with its mood visible through its body. Does not do small talk, but it is good company.
dex.fact: Many Antarctic fish make their own antifreeze proteins, which stop ice crystals growing in their blood.

species.real: Fish of the notothenioid group make up most of the fish living around Antarctica, having had the cold seas largely to themselves since their relatives died out or left.
